column2: Retain the repeated advance and siege rather than compressing the two clauses. The singular collective force, thirty-two accompanying kings and all the horse/chariot equipment are represented; son of Ader follows the selected form rather than substituting Ben-hadad.

Retain the incomplete sentence continuing into verse 3. The sender is the Syrian king from verse 1; Ahab is named as Israel's king and the destination is the city. No messengers are supplied here before their explicit appearance later.
Retain both assertions of possession and both groups, silver/gold and wives/children. The nested announcement has human you/your and does not add a qualification such as best children.

Retain lord king as human address and the first-person submission embracing the speaker and all his possessions. The opening comparison refers to what the Syrian king has said; no divine-address forms are appropriate.

Retain the returning messengers and the repeated first demand in direct speech. The Greek perfect sending is idiomatically narrated as I sent; the future give expresses the demand. The quotation continues into verse 6, so no final closing marks are supplied here.

Retain tomorrow at this time, the search of both the king's and his attendants' houses, and the desire of their eyes, not your eyes. The hands and taking remain plural and refer to the raiding attendants; the initial For represents the connecting hoti.

Retain the appeal to all the elders, the two commands understand/see, and the explicit wives, sons and daughters. The separate denial of withholding silver and gold remains; it is not rewritten to say that every earlier demand was already fulfilled.
Retain both prohibitions, listening and consenting, and both groups offering the advice. The two short clauses read naturally aloud while preserving their parallel force.

Retain the distinction between the first demands he will meet and this demand he cannot meet. Your servant remains the king's self-description within the message; the concluding return of the men and report are included.

Retain the singular god in the foreign king's oath and the selected foxes rather than replacing them with handfuls of dust. The relation of foxes to all the people, my foot soldiers, is genuinely difficult; the dash is editorial, not a settled explanation. The negative force of an oath introduced by if is not expanded into a confident numerical claim.
column3: What is the syntax and intended imagery of the foxes and foot soldiers, and how should the incomplete oath's polarity be expressed in natural English?

column2: Retain the initial Enough and the bent/upright contrast. The selected proverb does not mention putting armor on or taking it off; that familiar image must not be imported. Upright may be physical rather than moral, and its precise proverbial application remains open.
column3: Does bent/upright denote posture, preparedness or another proverbial contrast here?

column2: Retain the drinking of the king and all his fellow kings in tents, followed by the order to construct a siegework and its execution. The passive English opening avoids overidentifying the unexpressed subject of answered; the precise delivery of the reply remains implicit.

Retain both presentatives, the great crowd as the object delivered, today's timing, plural hands and the recognition formula. A prophet expresses the indefinite one prophet without implying a previously identified prophet; the Lord addresses the king with ordinary you.

Retain the two distinct questions, the young attendants of the district rulers as the means, and Ahab himself as the one to initiate the battle. Through whom interprets the instrumental en tini in light of the personal answer; the second reply is simply You.

Retain two hundred thirty attendants and sixty thousand men of valor. These are the selected figures, not seven thousand. The second muster follows the first and includes every son of strength, idiomatically every man of valor.

Retain noon and the repeated thirty-two allied kings. Socchoth follows the selected capitalized place form rather than silently substituting booths, although its relation to the tents of verse 12 is unresolved. Drinking himself drunk gives the ongoing drinking/intoxication sequence.
column3: Should Socchoth remain a place-name here, or does the selected form preserve a reference to booths/tents?

column2: Retain the young attendants going first and the report that men have emerged from Samaria. The Greek leaves the plural senders/reporters unnamed; the English They should not be treated as securely identifying the attendants as those who inform the Syrian king.
column3: How should the subject shift in they send and report be signaled without inventing scouts absent from this clause?

column2: Retain the repeated command to capture alive for both peaceful and hostile intentions. The speech remains open because the following selected prohibition belongs to its continuation in the inherited punctuation.

Retain the selected prohibition do not let ... come out, rather than converting it into the familiar positive narrative that they went out. The force behind them remains the grammatical lead-in to verse 20, with no period inserted at the unit boundary.
column3: The scope of the king's speech and the relation of the prohibition to the following attacking force need independent syntactic review.

column2: Retain the continuation of verse 19, each man's action, the repeated blow, Syria's flight and Israel's pursuit, and escape on a cavalryman's horse. Beside him follows par' autou but does not settle whether the intended victim is an opponent directly facing him or a companion; the second verb is also unusually expressed.
column3: Review the agents and victims in each struck the one beside him and each repeated, including whether repeated the blow overdefines the elliptical second verb.

column2: Retain the king's emergence, capture of all horses and chariots, and great defeat inflicted on Syria. The selected took is not replaced by destroyed, and all belongs to the captured equipment.

Retain the three imperatives about strength, understanding and consideration, followed by the return-of-the-year warning. Must do interprets the future what you will do as practical deliberation; no particular season or month is supplied.

Retain the Syrian speakers' claim about Israel's God, including the explicit not a God of valleys. Level ground interprets kat' euthy in the military contrast, and surely conveys the emphatic conditional/oath-like assurance. Capitalization identifies the reported referent without endorsing the speakers' theology.
column3: Is level ground the best contextual force of kat' euthy here, and is God or Israel the implicit subject of was stronger than we?

column2: Retain each king's dismissal to his own place and replacement with satraps. The selected office is not flattened into kings or generic soldiers, and no ethnic identity is added for the new commanders.

Propose you lost for you did lose in ordinary human speech. The replacement force, matching cavalry and chariots, renewed level-ground combat and promised superiority remain, as does the king's acceptance. The participle fallen from you is interpreted as military loss, not voluntary departure.

Retain the return of the year, the muster of Syria and the advance to Aphek for war against Israel. The place follows the selected Apheka form through the established English spelling; the text does not here specify which Aphek.

Retain Israel's muster and meeting of the enemy, the two flocks of goats comparison, and Syria filling the land. The small-force image is not made into two individual goats; the selected text does not include an extra statement about provisioning.

Retain the man of God designation, the repeated mountain/valley assertion, the Lord's reply and recognition formula. The force is delivered into singular hand here, unlike plural hands in verse 13; the divine speaker addresses the king with ordinary you.

Retain seven days facing one another, battle on the seventh day, and a hundred thousand Syrian foot soldiers struck in one day. No attempt is made to reduce or reconcile the selected numbers, and the reciprocal facing is naturalized as one another.

Retain the flight to Aphek, the wall falling on twenty-seven thousand survivors, and the Syrian king's further retreat into an inner chamber. The unusual house of the bedchamber wording tracks the selected double location without inventing a sequence of multiple rooms.
column3: What architectural relation is intended by house of the bedchamber into the inner chamber, and can it be expressed more naturally without losing a location?

column2: Retain the Syrian king as the speaker, I know rather than a report by his servants, and the inclusive proposal to put on sackcloth and ropes. Preserve our lives expresses the plural souls in this context without claiming a separate metaphysical sense.

Retain the sackcloth and ropes, the servant designation, the plea to live, and Ahab's question followed by brother. The singular life in the reported plea differs from the plural lives in verse 31; ordinary human address is maintained.

Retain the men's omen-taking and rapid repetition of brother, followed by the invitation, emergence and ascent into the chariot. The final plural they brought remains plural; it is not silently changed to Ahab personally lifting him.

Retain the promise of restored ancestral cities and outlets in Damascus, with the Samaria comparison. The quotation break before I will send you away marks an inferred change to Ahab, although the Greek does not add a new speaker label. Outlets leaves the scope of exodoi broader than explicitly commercial markets.
column3: Are exodoi streets, trading establishments or access rights, and where should the unmarked change of speaker be punctuated?

column2: Retain one of the sons of the prophets, his neighbor, the authority of the Lord's word, and the request followed by unwillingness. The refusal is represented as unwillingness rather than physical inability; no explanation for the requested blow is added.

Retain the causal rebuke for not listening, the presentative, the prediction that a lion will strike, and its narrative fulfillment. The selected final verb says struck rather than explicitly killed; the English does not add death.

Retain another man and the renewed polite request. Delivering a blow preserves the repeated strike construction, while bruising is provisional for the stronger synetripsen; the following bandage suggests injury but does not itself settle the severity.
column3: Does bruising understate synetripsen here; would injured or wounded preserve the force better without claiming broken bones?

column2: Retain the prophet standing on the road for the king and the bandage around his eyes. Waiting is a contextual expansion of stood for the king, not a separate Greek participle; the covering is not changed into ashes or a general facial disguise.

Retain the reported battlefield story as the prophet's speech, the man bringing another man, the guard command, and life-for-life or a talent of silver as alternatives. Weigh out preserves the payment image. If he escapes idiomatically compresses the repeated escape construction without weakening the condition.

Retain the servant's looking here and there and the disappearance, then the selected ambush/murder response. The awkward reply must not be replaced with the familiar assertion that the servant has pronounced his own judgment. Beside me for par' emoi is provisional; the logical relation of ambushes and murder remains unresolved.
column3: What does the king mean by the ambushes too and you murdered par' emoi; can a defensible natural rendering be established without replacing the selected reading?

column2: Retain the quick removal of the bandage from the eyes and the king's recognition that the man belongs to the prophets. The text does not identify him by name or say that this was the same prophet as in the earlier battle announcements.

Propose you let for you did let in the Lord's address to the king. The doomed man, release from the king's hand, life-for-life and people-for-people sanctions remain. Doomed is provisional for olethrion, whose destructive/disastrous sense should not be treated as a fully resolved technical ban term.
column3: Does olethrion describe a doomed man or a destructive man here, and does let ... out adequately express the active brought out verb?

column2: Retain both confounded and dispirited and the return to Samaria. The paired states are not replaced with angry merely to align with another account; the historic present comes is naturally narrated in the past.
